# Handoff — new skill: interface mapping spec (2026-10-15)

Start a fresh session with: "HANDOFF_2026-10-15_interface-mapping-spec.md 읽고 이어서 진행해줘".

## Goal (user's words, summarised)

A new sc4sap skill that asks the user a few questions and produces an **interface mapping specification** as an **editable HTML** page laid out like the user's Excel template. Editable-HTML behaviour should follow the existing skills (`program-to-manual`, `program-to-spec`, `config-to-document`). **The user wants to be asked** about open points and improvements — even small ones — before they are built.

## Template (reference only — local, customer file)

`C:\보관용\업무\한국타이어\기타\EAI_3030_매핑_정의서_CO00180_FUND CENTER 정보 송신_v0.1_20190625_암해.xlsx`

- Full dump (every cell, merges, validations, comments): `_handoff/interface-mapping-spec/dump.txt`; reader script `_handoff/interface-mapping-spec/read-xlsx.mjs <unzipped xlsx dir>` (unzip a *copy*: Copy-Item → .zip → Expand-Archive in the scratchpad).
- It is a real customer document (customer project name, vendor copyright, real people's names). The skill and anything public (repo, CHANGELOG, README) must stay generic: no customer / vendor names, no people. See memory `feedback_no_company_initials_in_docs`, `feedback_no_customer_specifics_in_changelog`.

### Sheets

1. **표지 (cover)** — project name, document title "인터페이스 매핑 정의서", document number `EAI-3030-인터페이스-매핑-정의서-<IF ID>`, "(<IF name>)", version, copyright lines (make all configurable).
2. **개정이력 (revision history)** — 순번 / 버전 / 변경 일자 / 변경 내용 / 작성자 / 승인자; note "변경이 발생되는 위치와 변경 내용을 자세히 기록".
3. **매핑 정의서 (mapping spec)** — 17 columns A–Q; `*` = required.
   - Header block: *인터페이스 ID, *인터페이스 명, *인터페이스 개요, 인터페이스 상세 설명, 전송방식 | *인터페이스 구동방식, *인터페이스 주기 | 인터페이스 주기 별 회수, 1회 전송 건수 | 건당 데이터 크기, 송/수신 시스템 관계 | *Target 기본 로직, *매핑 정의서 작성자 | *매핑 정의서 작성일.
   - Request block "Source System → Target System": per side *시스템 명, *모듈 명 (SAP: required), *지역, *시스템 담당자, *I/F Methods (Adapter), *Object, *Structure, *필수(반복) 구분; then the field grid: No (A01…) | Table | *Field | *Key | *Type | *Size | *Null | *Desc | **R** (conversion-rule id) | Table | *Field | *Key | *Type | *Size | *Null | **MAPPING** (source No) | *Desc.
   - Response block "Source ← Target" (sync return, B01…): same grid (example XSTAT / XMSGS).
   - Footer: 컬럼별 변환규칙 (R1, R2, …), 데이터 추출조건 (I/F query — select / update SQL), 특이사항, 기타.
   - Note in the sheet: one-way async interfaces go to a "비동기_케이스" tab (not present in this file).
4. **매핑 정의서 항목설명 (field guide)** — every item with required flag and explanation (good source for in-page help / tooltips).

### Code lists (dropdowns, from an external 공통코드 sheet; cached values)

- 지역: 한국, 구주, 미주, 아태, 인니, 중국, 헝가리, G.PI
- 구동방식: PUSH, PULL
- 주기: 년, 월, 주, 일, 시, 분, 초, 실시간, 수시(수동), 기타
- 데이터 타입: CHAR, NCHAR, VARCHAR, VARCHAR2, NVARCHAR2, NUMBER, FLOAT, INTEGER, LONG, DATE, TIMESTAMP, RAW, LONG RAW, BLOB, CLOB, NCLOB, BFILE
- 여부: Y, N
- 송수신 관계: 1:1, 1:N, N:1
- 필수(반복): 0:1, 0:N, 1:1, 1:N
- Structure: PARAMETER, STRUCTURE, TABLE
- 전송방식: 동기(Syncronous), 비동기(Asyncronous), 비동기 콜백(Asyncronous Call Back)
- Adapter: JDBC (Oracle), JDBC (MS-SQL), JDBC (Sybase), JDBC (DB2), ABAP Proxy, 웹서비스 (SOAP), FTP, SFTP, RFC, DB LINK, ETC

## Building blocks to reuse (read before designing)

- Editable pages: `scripts/manual/manual-editor.mjs` (Quill bubble, screenshots, undo, IndexedDB draft, Save → embedded source, `build-manual.mjs --import`), `scripts/spec/spec-editor.mjs` + `md-to-html.mjs --editable` + `html-to-md.mjs` + `spec-version.mjs` (versioned specs, history.json), `scripts/config/config-doc-editor.mjs` (plain-text fields, table cells/rows, `data-ef`/`data-ve` attributes, edits JSON in `<script id="config-edits">`, `--import` merge with newer-wins).
- Excel output exists: `scripts/spec/md-to-xlsx.mjs` (compare-programs).
- SAP side (optional auto-fill): MCP `GetStructure` / `GetTable` / `GetFunctionModule` / `GetDataElement` for SAP field names, types, lengths, descriptions of the source/target object (ABAP Proxy structure, RFC, Z table).
- Artifact paths: `common/multi-profile-artifact-resolution.md` (new category folder under the profile artifact base).

## Rules to keep

- Skill / agent MD ≤ 200 lines, English only (`feedback_md_line_limit`, `feedback_skill_md_language`); Agent dispatches use `sc4sap:sap-<name>`.
- Editable fields: plain text through `esc()`; table cells stay table cells (bug fixed in 0.6.37: no `display:block` on `td.ed`); undo, draft, save, import as in config-doc-editor.
- Release flow: tests (`npx vitest run`), tsc, version bump in package.json + plugin.json + marketplace.json (×2), CHANGELOG, commit on `active` with Entire trailer (`entire attach <session>` → `Entire-Checkpoint:`), push, merge to `main`, CI, 3-location sync (marketplace clone + cache `installPath`). `main` push currently bypasses a "PR required" rule — ask the user whether to keep doing that.

## Decisions (user, 2026-10-15) — questions 1–10 are answered

1. **Editable HTML only** — no `.xlsx` output.
2. **SAP fields auto-filled** — the SAP side (field, type, length, description, key) is read from SAP via MCP (DDIC structure / table, FM / proxy signature); the user fills the non-SAP side.
3. **One page**; the response block (Source ← Target, B01…) is an optional block on the same page (sync), not a separate layout.
4. **Yes** — cover page fields (project name, company, document-number pattern, copyright line) are configurable per project.
5. **Yes** — the cached code lists are defaults, with a per-project override.
6. **One interface per document.**
7. **English companion** page, like program-to-manual / compare-programs.
8. **Yes** — versioning v0.1 → v0.2 …, revision-history table filled on each save / import.
9. **Yes** — `/sc4sap:interface-mapping-spec` → `<artifactBase>/interfaces/<IF_ID>/`.
10. **Yes** — in-page validation: empty required (`*`) fields highlighted, MAPPING numbers checked against source rows, R ids checked against the conversion-rule list.

### Design decisions (user, 2026-10-15, second session)

11. SAP-side Type/Size: **converted to the DB type code list** (NUMC→NUMBER, DATS→DATE, …); the original DDIC type shown as a tooltip.
12. Non-SAP side: **pre-filled proposal** (same field names, converted types, MAPPING 1:1, marked "proposed") that the user corrects.
13. Extra validation warnings — all four: size truncation without an R rule, type-family mismatch without an R rule, target row with neither MAPPING nor R, key mismatch.
14. **`--refresh`**: re-read SAP, update only the SAP side, keep user content, mark added / removed / changed fields, new version +0.1 with a revision row.

---
name: interface-mapping-spec
description: Write an interface mapping specification as one editable HTML page in the classic template layout — cover, revision history, header, Source → Target field grid with conversion rules and MAPPING, optional synchronous response block, extraction condition, field guide. SAP side read from DDIC (table, structure, view, function module) or, for new interfaces, from a field list or the module consultant's proposal; non-SAP side proposed; in-page checks; versioned; English companion.
model: inherit
---

# SC4SAP Interface Mapping Specification

Interviews the consultant briefly and writes **one editable HTML page per interface**: cover, revision history, the mapping sheet (header, systems, Source → Target grid with R / MAPPING columns, response block for synchronous interfaces, conversion rules, extraction condition, remarks) and the field guide. The SAP side comes from the system; the other side is proposed and corrected in the page.

<Purpose>
Most mapping specifications are written for **new** interfaces, before any SAP object exists, by a consultant who has to fill dozens of type / length / description cells by hand. This skill fills everything SAP already knows, proposes the rest (counterpart fields, DB types, conversion rules, scenario defaults) and checks the result, so the consultant only decides what needs a decision.
</Purpose>

<Response_Prefix>Every response triggered by this skill MUST begin with `[Model: <main-model> · Dispatched: <sub-summary>]` per [`../../common/model-routing-rule.md`](../../common/model-routing-rule.md) § Response Prefix Convention.</Response_Prefix>

<Phase_Banner>Before each `Agent(...)` dispatch, emit `▶ phase=<id> (<label>) · agent=<name> · model=<Opus|Sonnet|Haiku>` per [`../../common/model-routing-rule.md`](../../common/model-routing-rule.md) § Phase Banner Convention. Resolve the dispatch mode first per [`../../common/model-dispatch-mode.md`](../../common/model-dispatch-mode.md).</Phase_Banner>

<Team_Mode>**No teamMode integration.** Reading SAP, proposing and building are scripted; agents only propose fields (optional) and translate.</Team_Mode>

<Use_When>
- "인터페이스 매핑 정의서", "매핑 스펙", "interface mapping spec", "I/F 정의서", "EAI 매핑", "field mapping for interface <ID>"
- A new interface must be specified before development (the usual case)
- An existing RFC / proxy structure / Z table needs its mapping written down
- An edited page comes back (import), or the SAP structure changed (refresh)
</Use_When>

<Do_Not_Use_When>
- Specification of a program → `/sc4sap:program-to-spec`
- Creating the Z structure / RFC itself → `/sc4sap:create-object` (this skill hands it the field list, Step 8)
- An interface catalogue across many interfaces — one interface per document
</Do_Not_Use_When>

<Decisions_Fixed>
Settled with the user when the skill was designed — do not ask again:

| Topic | Decision |
|---|---|
| Output | Editable HTML only (no `.xlsx`); one interface per document; one page with an optional response block (B01…) for synchronous interfaces |
| SAP side | Read from SAP (DDIC table / DB view / structure — a proxy by its structure —, CDS by SQL view name, function module signature). New interfaces: a `TABLE-FIELD` / data-element list, the module consultant's proposal (checked against DDIC), Excel paste in the page, or an empty grid |
| SAP types | Shown as DB types of the code list (NUMC → NUMBER, DATS → DATE …); the DDIC type is the cell tooltip |
| Other side | Proposed (same names, DB types, MAPPING 1:1), marked "Proposal" until edited or confirmed |
| Conversion rules | Proposed from the SAP types (date, time, leading zeros / ALPHA, currency, quantity / unit) and linked in the R column |
| Checks | Empty required (*) items, MAPPING to a missing row, unknown R id, size truncation, type-family mismatch, unmapped target field, key mismatch — all in the page's Checks panel |
| Versions | v0.1 → +0.1 per saved / imported edit, per refresh with changes; the revision-history table fills itself (author, change, optional approver) |
| Language | Page language from `.sc4sap/config.json` (`language`, else `ko`); English companion always built unless the user opts out |
| Settings | `<base>/interfaces/project.json`: cover (project name, title, document-number pattern `IF-MAP-{ifId}`, copyright), `idPattern` for IF ID numbering, code-list overrides (`codes`) |
| Location | `<base>/interfaces/<IF_ID>/` — `<base>` per [`../../common/multi-profile-artifact-resolution.md`](../../common/multi-profile-artifact-resolution.md) (`.sc4sap/work/<alias>/` with an active profile) |
| Template content | Generic: never put customer, vendor or people names into the skill or into public docs; real names belong only in the user's `project.json` and documents |
</Decisions_Fixed>

<Workflow>
`<B>` = `node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/interface/build-if-spec.mjs"`; every command prints one JSON line (`ok`, `html`, `version`, `findings`, `top`, `problems`). Never paste table contents or the whole model into chat.

**Entry check.** If the user hands back an edited page → Step 6. "Refresh / SAP changed" → Step 7. "Z structure / create the RFC" → Step 8. Otherwise a new document: Steps 1–5.

**Step 1 — Preflight and project settings.** Confirm the active profile in one line. If `<base>/interfaces/project.json` is missing, ask once (MUST read [`interview.md`](interview.md) § Project) and `Write` it.

**Step 2 — Interview.** MUST read [`interview.md`](interview.md) § Interface. One `AskUserQuestion` round (scenario preset, where the SAP fields come from, IF ID), then one short free-text ask for name, summary, systems and the SAP object or field list. Unanswered items stay empty — the page highlights them; do not chase every field in chat.

**Step 3 — Field proposal (only when the user chose "describe the business").** Dispatch the module consultant with [`dispatch-prompts.md`](dispatch-prompts.md) § 1. Show the returned `TABLE-FIELD` list with one reason each and ask the user to confirm or trim it in one message; the confirmed list becomes `fields`.

**Step 4 — Build v0.1.** `Write` the answers to `<base>/interfaces/_answers/<IF_ID>.json` (shape in `interview.md` § Answers), then `<B> init --answers <file>`. Report `problems` (fields SAP does not have, unreadable parameter types — for those offer `--line PARAM=STRUCTURE` and `refresh`).

**Step 5 — English companion.** Skip when the page language is `en` or the user opted out. `<B> texts --if <ID> --to en` → when `todo` > 0, dispatch `sc4sap:sap-writer` with [`dispatch-prompts.md`](dispatch-prompts.md) § 2 to write `outFile`; then `<B> companion --if <ID> --to en`. `missing` must be empty.

**Step 6 — Import an edited page.** `<B> import <file>` → new version with the reader's revision row; hand-typed SAP fields (`EKPO-MATNR`, data elements) are filled from DDIC at the same time (`resolved`, `problems`). Refusals: version already imported, or the page was edited from an older version (`--force` only when the user says to overwrite). `companionEdited: true` → tell the user edits belong in the primary-language page. Then Step 5 again.

**Step 7 — Refresh from SAP.** `<B> refresh --if <ID>` → `unchanged: true`, or a new version with added / changed / removed fields marked in the grid and a revision row. Then Step 5 again.

**Step 8 — Hand-off to create-object (on request, or offered once the user says the mapping is agreed).** `<B> fields --if <ID>` lists the SAP-side fields with data elements; offer `/sc4sap:create-object` for a Z structure (proxy / RFC) built from that list. Never create SAP objects from this skill.

**Close.** Report in the user's language: page path(s), version, findings (errors / warnings / to confirm) with the first few error texts, `problems`, and the next steps: open the page → **Edit** → **Save** → hand the file back for import.
</Workflow>

<Page>
Top bar: Checks (count; panel lists every finding, click jumps to the cell), Edit, Undo, Save, Print, link to the companion. Edit mode needs nothing installed: click a cell, pick code items from lists, paste a block of cells from Excel into the grid, add / insert / move / delete rows (No renumbered, MAPPING follows), ✓ confirms a proposal, add rules / SQL lines / revision rows, add or drop the response block, autosave in the browser. Save asks author, change and approver and downloads `<IF_ID>-v<next>-<lang>-edited.html`. Print: A4 landscape, one sheet per page.
</Page>

# Interview — Interface Mapping Specification

Referenced by `SKILL.md` Steps 1, 2 and 4. Keep it short: the consultant fills details faster in the page than in chat. Ask in the user's language; option labels below are English templates — translate them.

## Project (first run only — `<base>/interfaces/project.json` missing)

One `AskUserQuestion` with two questions, then one free-text ask:

1. **IF ID numbering** — options: `{module}{seq:5}` (e.g. SD00001) · `IF-{seq:4}` (e.g. IF-0001) · "No numbering, I give the ID each time". The user may type another pattern via Other (`{module}`, `{seq:N}`, fixed text).
2. **Region list** — options: "Default list (Korea, China, Asia-Pacific, Europe, Americas, Global)" (Recommended) · "Our own list" (ask for it in the free-text step).

Free text, one message: project name, document title (default: the template title in the page language), document-number pattern (default `IF-MAP-{ifId}`), copyright / confidentiality lines, own region list if chosen.

```json
{
  "projectName": { "ko": "…", "en": "…" },
  "title": { "ko": "인터페이스 매핑 정의서", "en": "Interface Mapping Specification" },
  "docNo": "IF-MAP-{ifId}",
  "copyright": ["…"],
  "idPattern": "{module}{seq:5}",
  "codes": { "region": ["…"] }
}
```

Any text may be a plain string or `{ ko, en }`. `codes` overrides any default list by name (`region`, `adapter`, `cycle`, `dataType`, `transfer`, `trigger`, `relation`, `cardinality`, `structure`); an entry is a string or `{ v, ko, en }`. Omit `codes` to keep the defaults. Never invent customer names.

## Interface (every new document)

**Round 1 — one `AskUserQuestion`, three questions:**

1. **Scenario** (pre-fills transfer mode, trigger, cycle, relation, target logic, structure, occurrence, response block):
   - Master data outbound — SAP → external, scheduled (`master-out`)
   - Transaction outbound — SAP document → external, on event (`txn-out`)
   - Inbound into SAP — external → SAP document, result returned (`inbound`)
   - Query — external system asks SAP, synchronous answer (`query`)
2. **SAP fields from** (decision 19):
   - An existing SAP object — table / view / structure / proxy structure / function module
   - A field list — `TABLE-FIELD` or data elements (e.g. `LIKP-VBELN, LIPS-MATNR, MEINS`)
   - Describe the business — the module consultant proposes the fields (Step 3)
   - Empty grid — fill or paste in the page
3. **IF ID** — when `idPattern` exists, run `<B> next-id --module <M>` first and offer the result as the first option "(Recommended)"; otherwise options "I'll type it" (Other). The module comes from the user's request or the active modules; ask inside this question's description if unclear.

**Round 2 — one free-text message** asking only what the round-1 answers left open:
- interface name and one-line summary
- the counterpart system (name, adapter if known) and the SAP system name as the project calls it
- the SAP object name, or the field list, or the business description (per question 2)
- author (name, contact) — reuse the previous document's author if there is one

Everything else (owners, region, cycle count, sizes, SQL, remarks) is filled in the page. Do not ask further rounds unless the SAP object cannot be found.

## Answers file (Step 4)

`<base>/interfaces/_answers/<IF_ID>.json`, written with `Write`:

```json
{
  "ifId": "SD00003",
  "module": "SD",
  "lang": "ko",
  "preset": "txn-out",
  "header": { "name": "…", "summary": "…", "author": "…" },
  "sides": {
    "source": { "system": "ERP", "module": "SD", "region": "KR", "adapter": "ABAP Proxy", "object": "…" },
    "target": { "system": "…", "region": "KR", "adapter": "JDBC (Oracle)" }
  },
  "objects": { "source": { "object": "ZSD_RFC_…", "kind": "FUNCTION" } },
  "fields": { "source": ["LIKP-VBELN", "LIPS-MATNR"] }
}
```

- `sapSide` follows the preset (`source` for outbound, `target` for inbound / query); set it only when the user says otherwise, or `both` for SAP-to-SAP.
- Give `objects` **or** `fields` for the SAP side, never both. `kind` is optional (`TABLE`, `STRUCTURE`, `VIEW`, `FUNCTION`); `lines: { "PARAM": "STRUCTURE" }` names line types the system cannot resolve (older releases).
- Leave `ifId` empty with `module` set to let `init` number it from `idPattern`.
- Header and side values for code lists use the stored codes: `transfer` SYNC / ASYNC / ASYNC_CB, `cycle` YEAR / MONTH / WEEK / DAY / HOUR / MIN / SEC / REALTIME / ADHOC / OTHER, `region` as in the region list (`v`), `trigger` PUSH / PULL.

# SC4SAP Interface Mapping Specification

Interviews the consultant briefly and writes **one editable HTML page per interface**: cover, revision history, the mapping sheet (header, systems, Source → Target grid with R / MAPPING columns, response block for synchronous interfaces, conversion rules, extraction condition, remarks) and the field guide. The SAP side comes from the system; the other side is proposed and corrected in the page.

<Purpose>
Most mapping specifications are written for **new** interfaces, before any SAP object exists, by a consultant who has to fill dozens of type / length / description cells by hand. This skill fills everything SAP already knows, proposes the rest (counterpart fields, DB types, conversion rules, scenario defaults) and checks the result, so the consultant only decides what needs a decision.
</Purpose>

<Response_Prefix>Every response triggered by this skill MUST begin with `[Model: <main-model> · Dispatched: <sub-summary>]` per [`../../common/model-routing-rule.md`](../../common/model-routing-rule.md) § Response Prefix Convention.</Response_Prefix>

<Phase_Banner>Before each `Agent(...)` dispatch, emit `▶ phase=<id> (<label>) · agent=<name> · model=<Opus|Sonnet|Haiku>` per [`../../common/model-routing-rule.md`](../../common/model-routing-rule.md) § Phase Banner Convention. Resolve the dispatch mode first per [`../../common/model-dispatch-mode.md`](../../common/model-dispatch-mode.md).</Phase_Banner>

<Team_Mode>**No teamMode integration.** Reading SAP, proposing and building are scripted; agents only propose fields (optional) and translate.</Team_Mode>

<Use_When>
- "인터페이스 매핑 정의서", "매핑 스펙", "interface mapping spec", "I/F 정의서", "EAI 매핑", "field mapping for interface <ID>"
- A new interface must be specified before development (the usual case)
- An existing RFC / proxy structure / Z table needs its mapping written down
- An edited page comes back (import), or the SAP structure changed (refresh)
</Use_When>

<Do_Not_Use_When>
- Specification of a program → `/sc4sap:program-to-spec`
- Creating the Z structure / RFC itself → `/sc4sap:create-object` (this skill hands it the field list, Step 8)
- An interface catalogue across many interfaces — one interface per document
</Do_Not_Use_When>

<Decisions_Fixed>
Settled with the user when the skill was designed — do not ask again:

| Topic | Decision |
|---|---|
| Output | Editable HTML only (no `.xlsx`); one interface per document; one page with an optional response block (B01…) for synchronous interfaces |
| SAP side | Read from SAP (DDIC table / DB view / structure — a proxy by its structure —, CDS by SQL view name, function module signature). New interfaces: a `TABLE-FIELD` / data-element list, the module consultant's proposal (checked against DDIC), Excel paste in the page, or an empty grid |
| SAP types | Shown as DB types of the code list (NUMC → NUMBER, DATS → DATE …); the DDIC type is the cell tooltip |
| Other side | Proposed (same names, DB types, MAPPING 1:1), marked "Proposal" until edited or confirmed |
| Conversion rules | Proposed from the SAP types (date, time, leading zeros / ALPHA, currency, quantity / unit) and linked in the R column |
| Checks | Empty required (*) items, MAPPING to a missing row, unknown R id, size truncation, type-family mismatch, unmapped target field, key mismatch — all in the page's Checks panel |
| Versions | v0.1 → +0.1 per saved / imported edit, per refresh with changes; the revision-history table fills itself (author, change, optional approver) |
| Language | Page language from `.sc4sap/config.json` (`language`, else `ko`); English companion always built unless the user opts out |
| Settings | `<base>/interfaces/project.json`: cover (project name, title, document-number pattern `IF-MAP-{ifId}`, copyright), `idPattern` for IF ID numbering, code-list overrides (`codes`) |
| Location | `<base>/interfaces/<IF_ID>/` — `<base>` per [`../../common/multi-profile-artifact-resolution.md`](../../common/multi-profile-artifact-resolution.md) (`.sc4sap/work/<alias>/` with an active profile) |

# Interview — Interface Mapping Specification

Referenced by `SKILL.md` Steps 1, 2 and 4. Keep it short: the consultant fills details faster in the page than in chat. Ask in the user's language; option labels below are English templates — translate them.

## Project (first run only — `<base>/interfaces/project.json` missing)

One `AskUserQuestion` with two questions, then one free-text ask:

1. **IF ID numbering** — options: `{module}{seq:5}` (e.g. SD00001) · `IF-{seq:4}` (e.g. IF-0001) · "No numbering, I give the ID each time". The user may type another pattern via Other (`{module}`, `{seq:N}`, fixed text).
2. **Region list** — options: "Default list (Korea, China, Asia-Pacific, Europe, Americas, Global)" (Recommended) · "Our own list" (ask for it in the free-text step).

Free text, one message: project name, document title (default: the template title in the page language), document-number pattern (default `IF-MAP-{ifId}`), copyright / confidentiality lines, own region list if chosen.

```json
{
  "projectName": { "ko": "…", "en": "…" },
  "title": { "ko": "인터페이스 매핑 정의서", "en": "Interface Mapping Specification" },
  "docNo": "IF-MAP-{ifId}",
  "copyright": ["…"],
  "idPattern": "{module}{seq:5}",
  "codes": { "region": ["…"] }
}
```

Any text may be a plain string or `{ ko, en }`. `codes` overrides any default list by name (`region`, `adapter`, `cycle`, `dataType`, `transfer`, `trigger`, `relation`, `cardinality`, `structure`); an entry is a string or `{ v, ko, en }`. Omit `codes` to keep the defaults. Never invent customer names.

## Interface (every new document)

**Round 1 — one `AskUserQuestion`, three questions:**

1. **Scenario** (pre-fills transfer mode, trigger, cycle, relation, target logic, structure, occurrence, response block):
   - Master data outbound — SAP → external, scheduled (`master-out`)
   - Transaction outbound — SAP document → external, on event (`txn-out`)
   - Inbound into SAP — external → SAP document, result returned (`inbound`)
   - Query — external system asks SAP, synchronous answer (`query`)
2. **SAP fields from** (decision 19):
   - An existing SAP object — table / view / structure / proxy structure / function module
   - A field list — `TABLE-FIELD` or data elements (e.g. `LIKP-VBELN, LIPS-MATNR, MEINS`)
   - Describe the business — the module consultant proposes the fields (Step 3)
   - Empty grid — fill or paste in the page
3. **IF ID** — when `idPattern` exists, run `<B> next-id --module <M>` first and offer the result as the first option "(Recommended)"; otherwise options "I'll type it" (Other). The module comes from the user's request or the active modules; ask inside this question's description if unclear.

**Round 2 — one free-text message** asking only what the round-1 answers left open:
- interface name and one-line summary
- the counterpart system (name, adapter if known) and the SAP system name as the project calls it
- the SAP object name, or the field list, or the business description (per question 2)
- author (name, contact) — reuse the previous document's author if there is one

Everything else (owners, region, cycle count, sizes, SQL, remarks) is filled in the page. Do not ask further rounds unless the SAP object cannot be found.

## Answers file (Step 4)

`<base>/interfaces/_answers/<IF_ID>.json`, written with `Write`:

```json
{
  "ifId": "SD00003",
  "module": "SD",
  "lang": "ko",
  "preset": "txn-out",
  "header": { "name": "…", "summary": "…", "author": "…" },
  "sides": {
    "source": { "system": "ERP", "module": "SD", "region": "KR", "adapter": "ABAP Proxy", "object": "…" },
    "target": { "system": "…", "region": "KR", "adapter": "JDBC (Oracle)" }
  },
  "objects": { "source": { "object": "ZSD_RFC_…", "kind": "FUNCTION" } },
  "fields": { "source": ["LIKP-VBELN", "LIPS-MATNR"] }
}
```

- `sapSide` follows the preset (`source` for outbound, `target` for inbound / query); set it only when the user says otherwise, or `both` for SAP-to-SAP.
- Give `objects` **or** `fields` for the SAP side, never both. `kind` is optional (`TABLE`, `STRUCTURE`, `VIEW`, `FUNCTION`); `lines: { "PARAM": "STRUCTURE" }` names line types the system cannot resolve (older releases).
- Leave `ifId` empty with `module` set to let `init` number it from `idPattern`.
- Header and side values for code lists use the stored codes: `transfer` SYNC / ASYNC / ASYNC_CB, `cycle` YEAR / MONTH / WEEK / DAY / HOUR / MIN / SEC / REALTIME / ADHOC / OTHER, `region` as in the region list (`v`), `trigger` PUSH / PULL.

-Before any work: verify `.sc4sap/config.json` exists and contains `sapVersion`, `abapRelease`, `industry`. Every recommendation, piece of generated code, and tool invocation must respect those fields.
-## Critical Rules (summary — full text in referenced files)

-2. **Match SAP version and ABAP release.** Never use S/4-only tables on ECC or syntax newer than the configured `abapRelease`. Full rules: `common/sap-version-reference.md`, `common/abap-release-reference.md`.

-3. **Transport discipline.** Every change goes on a transport. Description format: `[MODULE] [Action] [Object] - [brief]`. Never release with syntax errors or inactive objects. Every `CreateTransport` call must receive an explicit `client` parameter resolved from `.sc4sap/sap.env` SAP_CLIENT (full rule: `common/transport-client-rule.md`).

-4. **Activate after every change.** Run `GetAbapSemanticAnalysis` for syntax, then `GetInactiveObjects` to confirm no leftovers. Follow Clean ABAP conventions: `common/clean-code.md` (shared) + the paradigm-specific companion (`clean-code-oop.md` OR `clean-code-procedural.md`).

-5. **Data extraction is gated.** Before any `GetTableContents` / `GetSqlQuery`: consult `exceptions/table_exception.md` and `common/data-extraction-policy.md`. Schema/DDIC (`GetTable`, `GetStructure`, `GetView`, `GetDataElement`, `GetDomain`) is always allowed.

-6. **`acknowledge_risk` requires explicit user affirmative** (`yes` / `승인` / `authorize` / `approve` / `proceed` / `confirmed`). Ambiguous commands (`뽑아봐`, `try it`, `pull it`, `my mistake`) are NOT authorization. Per-call, per-table, per-session — never carries over. Full protocol: `common/data-extraction-policy.md` → "The `acknowledge_risk` Parameter — HARD RULE".

-7. **Industry context matters.** For config analysis / business process design / Fit-Gap: load the project's `industry/<key>.md` (from `config.json` → `industry` or `sap.env` → `SAP_INDUSTRY`). If unset, ask the user.

-8. **Country / localization context matters.** For tax, e-invoicing, banking, statutory reporting, date/number formats: load the project's `country/<iso>.md` (from `config.json` → `country` or `sap.env` → `SAP_COUNTRY`, ISO alpha-2 lowercase: `kr`, `us`, `de`, `eu-common`, …). +## Critical Rules (summary — full text in referenced files)

+2. **Match SAP version and ABAP release.** Never use S/4-only tables on ECC or syntax newer than the configured `abapRelease`. Full rules: `common/sap-version-reference.md`, `common/abap-release-reference.md`.

+3. **Transport discipline.** Every change goes on a transport. Description format: `[MODULE] [Action] [Object] - [brief]`. Never release with syntax errors or inactive objects. Every `CreateTransport` call must receive an explicit `client` parameter resolved from `.sc4sap/sap.env` SAP_CLIENT (full rule: `common/transport-client-rule.md`).

+4. **Activate after every change.** Run `GetAbapSemanticAnalysis` for syntax, then `GetInactiveObjects` to confirm no leftovers. Follow Clean ABAP conventions: `common/clean-code.md` (shared) + the paradigm-specific companion (`clean-code-oop.md` OR `clean-code-procedural.md`).

+5. **Data extraction is gated.** Before any `GetTableContents` / `GetSqlQuery`: consult `exceptions/table_exception.md` and `common/data-extraction-policy.md`. Schema/DDIC (`GetTable`, `GetStructure`, `GetView`, `GetDataElement`, `GetDomain`) is always allowed.

+6. **`acknowledge_risk` requires explicit user affirmative** (`yes` / `승인` / `authorize` / `approve` / `proceed` / `confirmed`). Ambiguous commands (`뽑아봐`, `try it`, `pull it`, `my mistake`) are NOT authorization. Per-call, per-table, per-session — never carries over. Full protocol: `common/data-extraction-policy.md` → "The `acknowledge_risk` Parameter — HARD RULE".

+7. **Industry context matters.** For config analysis / business process design / Fit-Gap: load the project's `industry/<key>.md` (from `config.json` → `industry` or `sap.env` → `SAP_INDUSTRY`). If unset, ask the user.

+8. **Country / localization context matters.** For tax, e-invoicing, banking, statutory reporting, date/number formats: load the project's `country/<iso>.md` (from `config.json` → `country` or `sap.env` → `SAP_COUNTRY`, ISO alpha-2 lowercase: `kr`, `us`, `de`, `eu-common`, …). Multi-country projects load every relevant file and flag cross-country touchpoints (intercompany, intra-EU VAT, transfer pricing). If unset, ask the user.

-Per-skill / per-phase model allocation across the sc4sap plugin. This document is the single source of truth for *which Claude model runs each step of each skill*, why that choice was made, and how the overrides work in practice.

-> **Scope**: all 13 user-facing skills + 16 agents. Companion planning docs, spec files, and per-phase rule files are not repeated here — see [`../skills/<name>/SKILL.md`](../skills) and [`../agents/`](../agents) for the primary sources. This doc summarizes the runtime model decisions they encode.

-sc4sap names tiers, not versions. Agent frontmatter uses the Claude Code aliases `haiku` / `sonnet` / `opus`, which track the newest model of each tier, so no file needs editing when a new model ships:
-| **Haiku** | `haiku` | Pure formatting, permission bootstrap, status diagnostics, trivial lookups, reference docs |
-| **Sonnet** | `sonnet` | Structured fact extraction, bulk template operations, reports |
-| **Opus** | `opus` | Novel code generation, cross-file reasoning, domain synthesis (module consultants), hypothesis narrowing, architecture design |

-Model choice follows [`common/model-routing-rule.md`](../common/model-routing-rule.md) § Tier decisions. The rule's core heuristic: **start at the lowest tier that can do the work correctly; escalate to Opus only for novel reasoning or ambiguity**.

-Every skill declares `model: inherit`, so the main thread runs on whatever model the session was opened with. The work that needs a specific tier is delegated to `Agent(...)` dispatches, which carry their own model (frontmatter alias or explicit override) — see § 3.
-Why no skill pins its main thread:

-- **The user's choice holds.** A host that opens a session on a chosen model (e.g. an Agent SDK web app) applies a skill's `model:` as a switch for the turn, so a pin silently replaced that choice. On CLI 2.1.283 the switch was registered but the replies still came from the session model (8 of 8 `model: haiku` invocations answered by Opus, 2026-09-28) — a pin was either overridden or ignored, never both useful and reliable.

-- **Prompt cache is per model.** Switching the main thread re-writes the whole cached context (system prompt + skill docs, ~26–46k tokens) for the new model. Measured 2026-09-27 on S/4HANA 758 through an Agent SDK host: `ask-consultant` pinned to Haiku cost $0.43 for a one-sentence answer, $0.28 of it the cache re-write; with `inherit` on a Haiku session the same question cost $0.09. `analyze-code` pinned to Sonnet cost more on a Haiku session ($0.79) than on a Sonnet one ($0.69).
-- **`trust-session` runs inside other skills.** Twelve skills invoke it mid-pipeline; a pin there would switch the model twice per pipeline and re-write the cache both times.

-A main-thread pin driven by a user preference (`~/.sc4sap/preferences.json`) is not offered: frontmatter `model:` is applied before the skill body runs, so a preference read at runtime cannot change it, and rewriting installed SKILL.md files would be undone by every plugin update.
-Suggested session model per skill (guidance only — nothing enforces it):
-| `trust-session` | any (inherits the caller) | Pure file editing + regex extraction, no domain judgment |
-| `sap-option` | Haiku or above | Interactive config editor, regex validation, secret masking |
-| `sap-doctor` | Haiku or above | 5-layer static checklist + structured PASS/FAIL report |
-| `mcp-setup` | Haiku or above | Reference documentation, optional `check` subcommand |
-| `ask-consultant` | Sonnet or above | Routing, teamMode divergence checks and synthesis review |
-| `setup` | Sonnet or above | Configuration workflow with failure triage and escalation |
-| `analyze-cbo-obj` | Sonnet or above | Orchestrates inventory analysis; synthesizes stocker output |
-| `analyze-code` | Sonnet or above | Orchestrates review; report composition needs judgment |
-| `analyze-symptom` | Sonnet or above | Routes questions, composes narratives from debugger output |
-| `compare-programs` | Sonnet or above | Orchestrates multi-program analysis; matrix assembly |
-| `config-to-document` | Sonnet or above | Runs the extract / notes / build scripts, batches the consultant-note dispatches, reports counts |
-| `create-object` | Sonnet or above | Metadata validation + executor/writer orchestration |
-| `create-program` | Sonnet or above | 9-phase pipeline orchestration, resume logic, state.json |
-| `package-to-process` | Sonnet or above | Entry-point detection, progress, per-process assembly and render |
-| `program-to-spec` | Sonnet or above | Socratic interview → structural inventory → analyst+writer delegation → render; depth / format / language state across turns |
-A Haiku session still works for the orchestration skills — the dispatched agents keep their own tiers — but multi-round state reconciliation and edge-case handling on the main thread are shallower.
-### Configuration / diagnostic skills (0 or conditional dispatches)
-Pure local file operations. No Agent calls.
-2 MCP reads (`GetSession`, `GetInactiveObjects`) for the status panel; rest is interactive editing.
-~15 MCP probes across 6 layers (plugin / MCP / SAP / required objects / config / RFC backend).
-Reference-doc renderer + optional `check` subcommand that shells out to `build-mcp-server.mjs --check`.
-Happy path on the main thread. Two conditional escalation paths:
-- **Step 4bis (RFC backend install) on error** → `sap-bc-consultant` (Opus) — pure Basis domain
-- **Steps 5–8 (connect/test) on error** → `general-purpose` with `model: "opus"` override — 3-layer diagnosis (SAP + MCP framework + Claude Code)
-Steps 11/11b (SPRO / customization extraction) are intentionally LLM-free: `scripts/extract-spro.mjs` and `scripts/extract-customizations.mjs` run as background Node processes.
-- Step 5 (conditional, ≥ 2 consultants) — `sap-writer` with `model: "sonnet"` override for cross-module synthesis

-- Steps 3–7 — `sap-stocker` (Sonnet) `MODE: walk` → `sap-checker` × N (Haiku, packages ≥ 30 objects) collect in-package callers + DDIC signals per batch → `sap-stocker` `MODE: finalize` scores, infers business purpose, checks cross-module gaps, persists (`skills/analyze-cbo-obj/stocker-fanout.md`; package-to-process Step 2 reuses it)
-- Step 8 (conditional, `Logic-heavy: true`) — main thread renders the briefing from `inventory.json` (no agent dispatch)
-- Step 2a — `sap-checker` (Haiku) size scout: source units, line counts, caller count

-- Step 2 — ≤ 1,500 lines: `sap-code-reviewer` (Opus) reads source + AST + semantic + where-used, evaluates 14 dimensions. > 1,500 lines: `sap-checker` × N (Haiku) detect candidates in 5 rule groups, then `sap-code-reviewer` (Opus) judges them + evaluates the judgment dimensions
-- Step 2d — `sap-checker` × N (Haiku) verify every finding's quoted evidence at its cited line; failures are reported as Unverified, not scored
-- Step 3 Branch B (conditional, Critical or ≥ 10 findings) — main thread renders the briefing (no agent dispatch)
-- Step 2 per round — `sap-debugger` with `model: "opus"` override for full investigation + hypothesis narrowing (dump + transport + code + enhancement + customization + profiler)
-- Step 3 — `sap-checker` × N (Haiku) — verbatim `FACT` extraction per program (per include batch when a program is too large)
-- Step 4 — `sap-analyst` × 1 (Opus) — consolidated module classify + dimension scoring + exec summary + recommendation
-- Step 5 — `sap-writer` × 1 (Sonnet override) — per-program screen specs + render, report `.md`; main thread builds the editable HTML page
-- Step 5.3 (when the report language ≠ en) — `sap-writer` × 1 (Sonnet override) — English companion
-#### `config-to-document` — session-model main, 2–3 dispatches per note batch
-- Steps 2–3, 5 — no agent: `scripts/config/extract-config.mjs` (background Node) reads the IMG tree, table values, transports and IMG documentation; `build-config-doc.mjs` renders the HTML
-- Step 4 write / revise — `sap-{module}-consultant` × 1 per batch (Opus, frontmatter; ≤ 4 batches in parallel) — consultant notes per IMG activity
-- Step 4 review — `sap-critic` × 1 per batch (Opus, frontmatter) — `ok` / `fix` verdict per note; one revise round for `fix` items
-- Step 4+5+6 (or 4-ECC) — `sap-executor` with `model: "opus"` override — create + novel implementation + activate
-- Step 7 — main thread renders the completion report from the executor return (ECC uses mandatory verbatim format; no agent dispatch)
-| 0 Preflight | main thread | session | platform.md + active-modules |
-| **3 Spec Writing** | `sap-writer` | **Opus** (override) | Spec is the most critical artifact |
-| 3.5 Execution Mode | main thread | session | user prompt + state.json |
-| 4 Implementation | `sap-executor` × 1–3 | Wave-dependent | DDIC/Classes/Main → Opus · Text/Screen → Sonnet per [`model-routing-rule.md`](../common/model-routing-rule.md) |
-| 6 Review | `sap-code-reviewer` × 4 buckets | Sonnet + Opus escalate | parallel buckets, MAJOR → Opus merge |
-| **8 Completion Report** | `sap-writer` | **Sonnet** (override) | Report composition from structured state |

-- Step 3 — `sap-analyst` (Opus, frontmatter) — business purpose + inputs/outputs + data sources + main logic narrative + auth checks + error cases (single dispatch covers all narrative dimensions; CBO-annotated when `cbo-context.md` preloaded)
-  - **L1 / L2 depth** → Haiku base (pure templating from analyst output)
-  - **L3 / L4 depth** → **Sonnet** override (`model: "sonnet"`) — longer narrative + deeper cross-reference + stronger consistency requirement
-- Step 3 (conditional, L4 only) — `sap-critic` (Opus, frontmatter) — verify every claim cross-references a concrete line range in source
-Excel output uses the same writer tier (depth-driven) — xlsx driver fill-in is mechanical; rendering depth determines tier, not format.
-### Pattern 1 — Main orchestrates, agent does heavy lifting

-Applied in every analysis / creation skill. Main thread holds only the structured return from agents, not their working memory (dump stack, source code, AST, where-used graph). Keeps orchestrator context small even for large objects / packages.

-Analyze-cbo-obj, analyze-code, ask-consultant branch between canned output (main thread formats directly) and rich briefing (dispatch to writer). Branching decision lives in the primary agent's return (`Logic-heavy`, consultant count) or, for analyze-code, in the verified finding counts after the Haiku evidence check.
-### Pattern 3 — Model override on agent dispatch
-The `Agent(...)` tool's `model` parameter overrides the agent's frontmatter. Used in:
-- `sap-executor` → Opus for novel code generation (`create-object`, `create-program` Wave 1/2.G2/3)
-- `general-purpose` → Opus for cross-layer diagnosis (`setup` Steps 5–8 escalation)
-Rationale: one agent can serve multiple skills at different model tiers without cloning the agent.

-Sonnet base + Opus escalate, per `common/model-routing-rule.md` § Escalation pattern. Agents return `BLOCKED` with context; skill re-dispatches at higher tier. Used in `create-program` Phase 6 (reviewer buckets) and `analyze-symptom` (debugger hypothesis narrowing).

-When the work is pure data extraction with no judgment (hundreds of MCP calls producing structured JSON), bypass the LLM entirely and run a background Node script. Used in `setup` Steps 11/11b (`extract-spro.mjs`, `extract-customizations.mjs`). Saves significant tokens on large modules.
-Every `/sc4sap:*` skill response starts with a **model prefix** indicating what ran where:
-Multi-phase skills additionally emit a **phase banner** before each dispatch:

-Rationale: users see cost and expertise levels in real time. Per-phase banners make model-routing decisions auditable. Spec lives in [`../common/model-routing-rule.md`](../common/model-routing-rule.md) § Response Prefix Convention and § Phase Banner Convention.
-When adding a new step or sub-agent, pick a tier by answering:
-1. **Does it generate novel ABAP code (a class body, FM signature, spec prose) or resolve cross-file ambiguity?** → **Opus**
-2. **Does it extract facts from structured inputs (AST, where-used, dumps) with rule-based matching?** → **Sonnet**
-3. **Is it pure string formatting from structured state, or permission / file bootstrap?** → **Haiku**

-If uncertain, start one tier lower and escalate on `BLOCKED`. Never start at Opus "just to be safe" — that defaults every new step to the most expensive tier and defeats the routing rule's cost-discipline goal.

+- Step 3 (new interface described in business terms) — `sap-{module}-consultant` × 1 (frontmatter model) — proposes `TABLE-FIELD` lines, each checked against DDIC
+- Step 5 (page language ≠ en) — `sap-writer` × 1 (Sonnet override) — translates only the texts not reused from earlier versions
+- Step 4+5+6 (or 4-ECC) — `sap-executor` with `model: "opus"` override — create + novel implementation + activate
+- Step 7 — main thread renders the completion report from the executor return (ECC uses mandatory verbatim format; no agent dispatch)
+| 0 Preflight | main thread | session | platform.md + active-modules |
+| **3 Spec Writing** | `sap-writer` | **Opus** (override) | Spec is the most critical artifact |
+| 3.5 Execution Mode | main thread | session | user prompt + state.json |
+| 4 Implementation | `sap-executor` × 1–3 | Wave-dependent | DDIC/Classes/Main → Opus · Text/Screen → Sonnet per [`model-routing-rule.md`](../common/model-routing-rule.md) |
+| 6 Review | `sap-code-reviewer` × 4 buckets | Sonnet + Opus escalate | parallel buckets, MAJOR → Opus merge |
+| **8 Completion Report** | `sap-writer` | **Sonnet** (override) | Report composition from structured state |

+- Step 3 — `sap-analyst` (Opus, frontmatter) — business purpose + inputs/outputs + data sources + main logic narrative + auth checks + error cases (single dispatch covers all narrative dimensions; CBO-annotated when `cbo-context.md` preloaded)
+  - **L1 / L2 depth** → Haiku base (pure templating from analyst output)
+  - **L3 / L4 depth** → **Sonnet** override (`model: "sonnet"`) — longer narrative + deeper cross-reference + stronger consistency requirement
+- Step 3 (conditional, L4 only) — `sap-critic` (Opus, frontmatter) — verify every claim cross-references a concrete line range in source
+Excel output uses the same writer tier (depth-driven) — xlsx driver fill-in is mechanical; rendering depth determines tier, not format.
+### Pattern 1 — Main orchestrates, agent does heavy lifting

+Applied in every analysis / creation skill. Main thread holds only the structured return from agents, not their working memory (dump stack, source code, AST, where-used graph). Keeps orchestrator context small even for large objects / packages.

+Analyze-cbo-obj, analyze-code, ask-consultant branch between canned output (main thread formats directly) and rich briefing (dispatch to writer). Branching decision lives in the primary agent's return (`Logic-heavy`, consultant count) or, for analyze-code, in the verified finding counts after the Haiku evidence check.
+### Pattern 3 — Model override on agent dispatch
+The `Agent(...)` tool's `model` parameter overrides the agent's frontmatter. Used in:
+- `sap-executor` → Opus for novel code generation (`create-object`, `create-program` Wave 1/2.G2/3)
+- `general-purpose` → Opus for cross-layer diagnosis (`setup` Steps 5–8 escalation)
+Rationale: one agent can serve multiple skills at different model tiers without cloning the agent.

+Sonnet base + Opus escalate, per `common/model-routing-rule.md` § Escalation pattern. Agents return `BLOCKED` with context; skill re-dispatches at higher tier. Used in `create-program` Phase 6 (reviewer buckets) and `analyze-symptom` (debugger hypothesis narrowing).

+When the work is pure data extraction with no judgment (hundreds of MCP calls producing structured JSON), bypass the LLM entirely and run a background Node script. Used in `setup` Steps 11/11b (`extract-spro.mjs`, `extract-customizations.mjs`). Saves significant tokens on large modules.
+Every `/sc4sap:*` skill response starts with a **model prefix** indicating what ran where:
+Multi-phase skills additionally emit a **phase banner** before each dispatch:

+Rationale: users see cost and expertise levels in real time. Per-phase banners make model-routing decisions auditable. Spec lives in [`../common/model-routing-rule.md`](../common/model-routing-rule.md) § Response Prefix Convention and § Phase Banner Convention.
+When adding a new step or sub-agent, pick a tier by answering:
+1. **Does it generate novel ABAP code (a class body, FM signature, spec prose) or resolve cross-file ambiguity?** → **Opus**
+2. **Does it extract facts from structured inputs (AST, where-used, dumps) with rule-based matching?** → **Sonnet**
+3. **Is it pure string formatting from structured state, or permission / file bootstrap?** → **Haiku**

+If uncertain, start one tier lower and escalate on `BLOCKED`. Never start at Opus "just to be safe" — that defaults every new step to the most expensive tier and defeats the routing rule's cost-discipline goal.

# Handoff — new skill: interface mapping spec (2026-10-15)

Start a fresh session with: "HANDOFF_2026-10-15_interface-mapping-spec.md 읽고 이어서 진행해줘".

## Goal (user's words, summarised)

A new sc4sap skill that asks the user a few questions and produces an **interface mapping specification** as an **editable HTML** page laid out like the user's Excel template. Editable-HTML behaviour should follow the existing skills (`program-to-manual`, `program-to-spec`, `config-to-document`). **The user wants to be asked** about open points and improvements — even small ones — before they are built.

## Template (reference only — local, customer file)

`C:\보관용\업무\한국타이어\기타\EAI_3030_매핑_정의서_CO00180_FUND CENTER 정보 송신_v0.1_20190625_암해.xlsx`

- Full dump (every cell, merges, validations, comments): `_handoff/interface-mapping-spec/dump.txt`; reader script `_handoff/interface-mapping-spec/read-xlsx.mjs <unzipped xlsx dir>` (unzip a *copy*: Copy-Item → .zip → Expand-Archive in the scratchpad).
- It is a real customer document (customer project name, vendor copyright, real people's names). The skill and anything public (repo, CHANGELOG, README) must stay generic: no customer / vendor names, no people. See memory `feedback_no_company_initials_in_docs`, `feedback_no_customer_specifics_in_changelog`.

### Sheets

1. **표지 (cover)** — project name, document title "인터페이스 매핑 정의서", document number `EAI-3030-인터페이스-매핑-정의서-<IF ID>`, "(<IF name>)", version, copyright lines (make all configurable).
2. **개정이력 (revision history)** — 순번 / 버전 / 변경 일자 / 변경 내용 / 작성자 / 승인자; note "변경이 발생되는 위치와 변경 내용을 자세히 기록".
3. **매핑 정의서 (mapping spec)** — 17 columns A–Q; `*` = required.
   - Header block: *인터페이스 ID, *인터페이스 명, *인터페이스 개요, 인터페이스 상세 설명, 전송방식 | *인터페이스 구동방식, *인터페이스 주기 | 인터페이스 주기 별 회수, 1회 전송 건수 | 건당 데이터 크기, 송/수신 시스템 관계 | *Target 기본 로직, *매핑 정의서 작성자 | *매핑 정의서 작성일.
   - Request block "Source System → Target System": per side *시스템 명, *모듈 명 (SAP: required), *지역, *시스템 담당자, *I/F Methods (Adapter), *Object, *Structure, *필수(반복) 구분; then the field grid: No (A01…) | Table | *Field | *Key | *Type | *Size | *Null | *Desc | **R** (conversion-rule id) | Table | *Field | *Key | *Type | *Size | *Null | **MAPPING** (source No) | *Desc.
   - Response block "Source ← Target" (sync return, B01…): same grid (example XSTAT / XMSGS).
   - Footer: 컬럼별 변환규칙 (R1, R2, …), 데이터 추출조건 (I/F query — select / update SQL), 특이사항, 기타.
   - Note in the sheet: one-way async interfaces go to a "비동기_케이스" tab (not present in this file).
4. **매핑 정의서 항목설명 (field guide)** — every item with required flag and explanation (good source for in-page help / tooltips).

### Code lists (dropdowns, from an external 공통코드 sheet; cached values)

- 지역: 한국, 구주, 미주, 아태, 인니, 중국, 헝가리, G.PI
- 구동방식: PUSH, PULL
- 주기: 년, 월, 주, 일, 시, 분, 초, 실시간, 수시(수동), 기타
- 데이터 타입: CHAR, NCHAR, VARCHAR, VARCHAR2, NVARCHAR2, NUMBER, FLOAT, INTEGER, LONG, DATE, TIMESTAMP, RAW, LONG RAW, BLOB, CLOB, NCLOB, BFILE
- 여부: Y, N
- 송수신 관계: 1:1, 1:N, N:1

---
name: interface-mapping-spec
description: Write an interface mapping specification as one editable HTML page in the classic template layout — cover, revision history, header, Source → Target field grid with conversion rules and MAPPING, optional synchronous response block, extraction condition, field guide. SAP side read from DDIC (table, structure, view, function module) or, for new interfaces, from a field list or the module consultant's proposal; non-SAP side proposed; in-page checks; versioned; English companion.
model: inherit
---

# SC4SAP Interface Mapping Specification

Interviews the consultant briefly and writes **one editable HTML page per interface**: cover, revision history, the mapping sheet (header, systems, Source → Target grid with R / MAPPING columns, response block for synchronous interfaces, conversion rules, extraction condition, remarks) and the field guide. The SAP side comes from the system; the other side is proposed and corrected in the page.

<Purpose>
Most mapping specifications are written for **new** interfaces, before any SAP object exists, by a consultant who has to fill dozens of type / length / description cells by hand. This skill fills everything SAP already knows, proposes the rest (counterpart fields, DB types, conversion rules, scenario defaults) and checks the result, so the consultant only decides what needs a decision.
</Purpose>

<Response_Prefix>Every response triggered by this skill MUST begin with `[Model: <main-model> · Dispatched: <sub-summary>]` per [`../../common/model-routing-rule.md`](../../common/model-routing-rule.md) § Response Prefix Convention.</Response_Prefix>

<Phase_Banner>Before each `Agent(...)` dispatch, emit `▶ phase=<id> (<label>) · agent=<name> · model=<Opus|Sonnet|Haiku>` per [`../../common/model-routing-rule.md`](../../common/model-routing-rule.md) § Phase Banner Convention. Resolve the dispatch mode first per [`../../common/model-dispatch-mode.md`](../../common/model-dispatch-mode.md).</Phase_Banner>

<Team_Mode>**No teamMode integration.** Reading SAP, proposing and building are scripted; agents only propose fields (optional) and translate.</Team_Mode>

<Use_When>
- "인터페이스 매핑 정의서", "매핑 스펙", "interface mapping spec", "I/F 정의서", "EAI 매핑", "field mapping for interface <ID>"
- A new interface must be specified before development (the usual case)
- An existing RFC / proxy structure / Z table needs its mapping written down
- An edited page comes back (import), or the SAP structure changed (refresh)
</Use_When>

<Do_Not_Use_When>
- Specification of a program → `/sc4sap:program-to-spec`
- Creating the Z structure / RFC itself → `/sc4sap:create-object` (this skill hands it the field list, Step 8)
- An interface catalogue across many interfaces — one interface per document
</Do_Not_Use_When>

<Decisions_Fixed>
Settled with the user when the skill was designed — do not ask again:

| Topic | Decision |
|---|---|
| Output | Editable HTML only (no `.xlsx`); one interface per document; one page with an optional response block (B01…) for synchronous interfaces |
| SAP side | Read from SAP (DDIC table / DB view / structure — a proxy by its structure —, CDS by SQL view name, function module signature). New interfaces: a `TABLE-FIELD` / data-element list, the module consultant's proposal (checked against DDIC), Excel paste in the page, or an empty grid |
| SAP types | Shown as DB types of the code list (NUMC → NUMBER, DATS → DATE …); the DDIC type is the cell tooltip |
| Other side | Proposed (same names, DB types, MAPPING 1:1), marked "Proposal" until edited or confirmed |
| Conversion rules | Proposed from the SAP types (date, time, leading zeros / ALPHA, currency, quantity / unit) and linked in the R column |
| Checks | Empty required (*) items, MAPPING to a missing row, unknown R id, size truncation, type-family mismatch, unmapped target field, key mismatch — all in the page's Checks panel |
| Versions | v0.1 → +0.1 per saved / imported edit, per refresh with changes; the revision-history table fills itself (author, change, optional approver) |
| Language | Page language from `.sc4sap/config.json` (`language`, else `ko`); English companion always built unless the user opts out |

`/sc4sap:interface-mapping-spec` 스킬 구현과 테스트를 마쳤습니다. 커밋과 릴리스는 아직 하지 않았습니다.

**확인한 결과**
- **자동 테스트**: vitest 482개 전부 통과, tsc 오류 없음.
- **편집 모드**: 헤드리스 Chrome에서 실제 페이지로 16개 항목을 확인했습니다. 칸 수정, 목록 선택, 행 삭제 후 번호와 MAPPING 갱신, Excel 붙여넣기, 되돌리기, 임시 저장, 저장 다운로드가 모두 동작합니다.
- **HKT-DEV 실제 시스템**: 말씀하신 ZSD008의 `ZSD_RFC*` 함수 3개를 무작위로 골라 시그니처를 해석했습니다. 한국어 설명까지 채워졌고, `OH_TAB`/`OI_TAB`은 응답 블록으로 나뉘었습니다. `LIKP-VBELN` 같은 필드 목록 조회도 동작했습니다.
- **명령 흐름**: 생성, 페이지 편집 후 import(직접 입력한 SAP 필드를 DDIC에서 자동으로 채움), 재동기화, IF ID 채번, 영문 페이지까지 모두 확인했습니다. 결과물은 scratchpad에만 썼습니다.
- **독립 리뷰**: 작성과 분리된 리뷰어가 결함 9건과 작은 문제 4건을 찾았고, 모두 고친 뒤 회귀 테스트를 추가했습니다. 주요 결함은 다음과 같았습니다.
  - 재동기화할 때 사용자가 쓴 설명이 SAP 값으로 덮어써짐
  - 양쪽이 SAP인 경우 재동기화 표시가 서로 지워짐
  - import한 페이지의 버전 값으로 다른 경로에 파일을 쓸 수 있었음
  - 저장을 두 번 하면 import가 거부됨

**신규 인터페이스용 편의 기능**
- 시나리오 프리셋 4종: 마스터 송신, 트랜잭션 송신, SAP 수신 처리, 조회. 고르면 헤더와 응답 블록이 미리 채워집니다.
- SAP 측 필드를 정하는 방법은 네 가지입니다. `TABLE-FIELD` 목록 입력, 업무 설명을 주면 모듈 컨설턴트 에이전트가 제안(DDIC로 존재 확인), Excel에서 붙여넣기, 빈 그리드.
- 변환규칙이 자동으로 제안되고 해당 행에 연결됩니다. 대상은 날짜, 시간, 앞자리 0(ALPHA), 통화 금액, 수량·단위입니다.
- 매핑이 확정되면 Z 구조 생성에 쓸 필드 목록을 뽑아 `/sc4sap:create-object`로 넘길 수 있습니다. 스킬이 SAP 객체를 직접 만들지는 않습니다.

**ECC에서 확인한 제약 두 가지**
- **DB 뷰**: `GetView`가 실패하지만 `GetTable`로 읽으면 됩니다. 스크립트는 그렇게 처리합니다.
- **테이블 타입 파라미터**: 라인 구조를 시스템에서 읽을 수 없습니다. 이름 규칙(`_T`, `_TAB`)으로 추정하고, 그래도 안 되면 `--line PARAM=STRUCTURE`로 지정합니다. 지정한 값은 다음 재동기화에도 유지됩니다.

직접 열어 보실 수 있는 샘플 페이지입니다. 신규 건 방식(필드 목록)으로 만들었고 v0.2입니다.
`C:\Users\pssps\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-pssps-Documents-Projects-sc4sap-project\9fb9c4c9-3f63-4909-abdf-09353de10774\scratchpad\ifs\SD00002\SD00002-v0.2-ko.html`

진행 상황은 핸드오프의 § Status와 메모리에 기록해 두었습니다.

**릴리스 여부를 정해 주세요.** 진행하면 0.6.38로 버전을 올리고, CHANGELOG 작성, Entire 트레일러를 붙여 `active`에 커밋한 뒤 `main` 병합, CI 확인, 3곳 동기화까지 하겠습니다. 이전처럼 "PR 필수" 규칙을 우회해 `main`에 직접 push해도 되는지도 함께 알려 주세요. 먼저 샘플 페이지를 보신 뒤 수정할 점을 말씀하셔도 됩니다.

- **RFC**: `I_TAB`처럼 그 필드가 실려 가는 파라미터가 들어갑니다.

name: interface-mapping-spec
description: Write an interface mapping specification as one editable HTML page in the classic template layout — cover, revision history, header, Source → Target field grid with conversion rules and MAPPING, optional synchronous response block, extraction condition, field guide. SAP side read from DDIC (table, structure, view, function module) or, for new interfaces, from a field list or the module consultant's proposal; non-SAP side proposed; in-page checks; versioned; English companion.

# SC4SAP Interface Mapping Specification

Interviews the consultant briefly and writes **one editable HTML page per interface**: cover, revision history, the mapping sheet (header, systems, Source → Target grid with R / MAPPING columns, response block for synchronous interfaces, conversion rules, extraction condition, remarks) and the field guide. The SAP side comes from the system; the other side is proposed and corrected in the page.

<Purpose>
Most mapping specifications are written for **new** interfaces, before any SAP object exists, by a consultant who has to fill dozens of type / length / description cells by hand. This skill fills everything SAP already knows, proposes the rest (counterpart fields, DB types, conversion rules, scenario defaults) and checks the result, so the consultant only decides what needs a decision.
</Purpose>

<Response_Prefix>Every response triggered by this skill MUST begin with `[Model: <main-model> · Dispatched: <sub-summary>]` per [`../../common/model-routing-rule.md`](../../common/model-routing-rule.md) § Response Prefix Convention.</Response_Prefix>

<Phase_Banner>Before each `Agent(...)` dispatch, emit `▶ phase=<id> (<label>) · agent=<name> · model=<Opus|Sonnet|Haiku>` per [`../../common/model-routing-rule.md`](../../common/model-routing-rule.md) § Phase Banner Convention. Resolve the dispatch mode first per [`../../common/model-dispatch-mode.md`](../../common/model-dispatch-mode.md).</Phase_Banner>

<Team_Mode>**No teamMode integration.** Reading SAP, proposing and building are scripted; agents only propose fields (optional) and translate.</Team_Mode>

<Use_When>
- "인터페이스 매핑 정의서", "매핑 스펙", "interface mapping spec", "I/F 정의서", "EAI 매핑", "field mapping for interface <ID>"
- A new interface must be specified before development (the usual case)
- An existing RFC / proxy structure / Z table needs its mapping written down
- An edited page comes back (import), or the SAP structure changed (refresh)
</Use_When>

<Do_Not_Use_When>
- Specification of a program → `/sc4sap:program-to-spec`
- Creating the Z structure / RFC itself → `/sc4sap:create-object` (this skill hands it the field list, Step 8)
- An interface catalogue across many interfaces — one interface per document
</Do_Not_Use_When>

<Decisions_Fixed>
Settled with the user when the skill was designed — do not ask again:

| Topic | Decision |
|---|---|
| Output | Editable HTML only (no `.xlsx`); one interface per document; one page with an optional response block (B01…) for synchronous interfaces |

| SAP types | Shown as DB types of the code list (NUMC → NUMBER, DATS → DATE …); the DDIC type is the cell tooltip |

`<B>` = `node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/interface/build-if-spec.mjs"` (`<PLUGIN_ROOT>` = two levels above this skill folder), run from the project root so the artifact base resolves; every command prints one JSON line (`ok`, `html`, `version`, `findings`, `top`, `problems`). Never paste table contents or the whole model into chat.

**Entry check.** If the user hands back an edited page → Step 6. "Refresh / SAP changed" → Step 7. "Z structure / create the RFC" → Step 8. Otherwise a new document: Steps 1–5.

**Step 1 — Preflight and project settings.** Confirm the active profile in one line. If `<base>/interfaces/project.json` is missing, ask once (MUST read [`interview.md`](interview.md) § Project) and `Write` it.

**Step 2 — Interview.** MUST read [`interview.md`](interview.md) § Interface. One `AskUserQuestion` round (scenario preset, where the SAP fields come from, IF ID), then one short free-text ask for name, summary, systems and the SAP object or field list. Unanswered items stay empty — the page highlights them; do not chase every field in chat.

**Step 3 — Field proposal (only when the user chose "describe the business").** Dispatch the module consultant with [`dispatch-prompts.md`](dispatch-prompts.md) § 1. Show the returned `TABLE-FIELD` list with one reason each and ask the user to confirm or trim it in one message; the confirmed list becomes `fields`.

**Step 4 — Build v0.1.** `Write` the answers to `<base>/interfaces/_answers/<IF_ID>.json` (shape in `interview.md` § Answers), then `<B> init --answers <file>`. Report `problems` (fields SAP does not have, unreadable parameter types — for those offer `--line PARAM=STRUCTURE` and `refresh`).

**Step 5 — English companion.** Skip when the page language is `en` or the user opted out. `<B> texts --if <ID> --to en` → when `todo` > 0, dispatch `sc4sap:sap-writer` with [`dispatch-prompts.md`](dispatch-prompts.md) § 2 to write `outFile`; then `<B> companion --if <ID> --to en`. `missing` must be empty.

**Step 6 — Import an edited page.** `<B> import <file>` → new version with the reader's revision row; hand-typed SAP fields (`EKPO-MATNR`, data elements) are filled from DDIC at the same time (`resolved`, `problems`). Refusals: version already imported; the page was edited from an older version (`--force` only when the user says to overwrite); an English companion page (edits go into the primary-language page, the companion is rebuilt from it); a page whose ID / version / language was changed outside edit mode. Then Step 5 again.

**Step 7 — Refresh from SAP.** `<B> refresh --if <ID> [--line PARAM=STRUCTURE]` → `unchanged: true`, or a new version with added / changed / removed fields marked in the grid and a revision row. Only SAP facts (type, length, DDIC type) are updated; key, null and descriptions the user wrote stay. `--line` values are remembered for later refreshes. Then Step 5 again.

**Step 8 — Hand-off to create-object (on request, or offered once the user says the mapping is agreed).** `<B> fields --if <ID>` lists the SAP-side fields with data elements; offer `/sc4sap:create-object` for a Z structure (proxy / RFC) built from that list. Table과 Structure의 구분을 그룹 행 방식으로 바꿨고, Source와 Target의 배경색도 다르게 했습니다. 아직 커밋하지 않았습니다.

**바뀐 점**
- **그룹 행(▸)**: 필드를 실어 나르는 단위(파라미터, 구조, 테이블)마다 그리드에 그룹 행이 생깁니다.
  - 그룹 행에는 Source와 Target 각각의 이름, 구분, 필수(반복)를 적습니다.
  - 예를 들어 RFC `ZSD_RFC_SHIPMENT_CHANGE`는 요청에 `▸ I_TAB · TABLE · 1:N (ZSDS10070)`, 응답에 `▸ OH_TAB`와 `▸ OI_TAB`가 각각 그룹으로 나뉩니다.
  - FM의 스칼라 파라미터는 방향별로 하나의 PARAMETER 그룹에 묶입니다.
- **행의 Table 칸**: 원천 DDIC 테이블(`EKPO` 등)만 넣습니다. 더 이상 파라미터 이름이 섞이지 않습니다.
- **시스템 블록의 Structure / 필수(반복)**: 직접 입력하지 않고 그룹에서 자동으로 요약합니다. 예: `TABLE 1:N (OH_TAB), TABLE 1:N (OI_TAB)`.
- **편집 모드**: 그룹 행의 이름은 직접 입력하고, 구분과 필수(반복)는 목록에서 고릅니다.
  - 그룹마다 행 추가와 그룹 삭제가 있고, 그리드 아래에 "+ 그룹 추가"가 있습니다.
  - 행 이동은 같은 그룹 안에서만 됩니다. Excel 붙여넣기로 생긴 행은 붙여넣은 칸의 그룹에 들어갑니다.
- **검증**: 필드가 있는 그룹의 구분과 필수(반복)가 비어 있으면 오류입니다. STRUCTURE와 TABLE 그룹은 이름이 비어 있어도 오류로 표시됩니다.
- **색**: Source는 파란색, Target은 초록색입니다. 그리드 헤더, 시스템 블록, 셀 배경에 모두 적용했습니다. 자동 제안된 쪽의 값은 기울임체 파란 글씨로 구분됩니다.

- **자동 테스트**: vitest 483개 전부 통과, tsc 오류 없음.

description: When making git commits in sc4sap_project, MUST include `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` trailer to keep entire session tracking intact
type: feedback
originSessionId: 21e03650-294e-4f69-aaef-74c569183474

When creating any `git commit` in `sc4sap_project` (or any repo where `entire` is enabled), the commit message MUST include an `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` trailer in the trailer block (next to / below `Co-Authored-By:`).

**Why:** `entire attach <session-id>` only registers checkpoint metadata in entire's DB and prints "Copy to your commit message to attach: Entire-Checkpoint: <id>". It does NOT automatically amend the commit to add the trailer (because last commit may already be pushed). The trailer is the chain mechanism — without it on a commit, entire's session ↔ commit linkage breaks for that commit and every subsequent one in the chain.

**How to apply:**
- Before authoring a commit, run `entire sessions list` (or `entire status`) and grab the active session's `checkpoint <id>` field.
- Append `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` as a trailer line in the commit message, on its own line in the trailer block.
- Reuse the same checkpoint ID for every commit in the same Claude Code session — `entire attach` only mints a new checkpoint when there's no checkpoint registered for the session yet.
- If the project active branch is shared (NO force-push policy) and a commit was already pushed without the trailer, do NOT try to fix via `entire attach` afterwards — it will `git commit --amend` the last commit silently and rewrite hash, forcing a reset-to-origin to recover.

**Real incident (2026-04-26):** Commit 1f4c5bf (program-to-spec PNG path fix) was authored without the trailer despite user having run `entire attach 21e03650...` earlier in the session. Result: trailer-less commit pushed to active/backup/main, and a follow-up `entire attach` silently amended local 1f4c5bf → f7615b7 forcing a hash divergence that had to be reset (force-push blocked by shared-branch policy). Net effect: that commit is permanently un-tracked by entire on origin.

**Safe pattern when the session has no checkpoint yet (worked 2026-09-30):** commit first (unpushed), then `entire attach <session-id> -f` — it amends only that unpushed commit with the trailer and mints the checkpoint; reuse the ID for later commits/merge. Never attach while HEAD is an already-pushed commit.

# Changelog

All notable changes to **SuperClaude for SAP (sc4sap)** will be documented in this file.
Format follows [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/); versioning follows [SemVer](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

## [0.6.37] — 2026-10-15

### Added — `config-to-document`: edit mode covers the views

- Edit mode now also edits each view card: its title, the value-table cells (rows added or deleted) and the change-history rows (added, edited, deleted). Edited views get the "Edited · author · date" badge, so readers see where the page differs from the system.
- A drawn SM30 screen (overview or detail) can be replaced by a real screenshot in edit mode — button, or click the drawing and Ctrl+V — and switched back to the drawing; captures wider than 1800 px are scaled down, only `data:image/…` sources are drawn.
- Editable table cells stay table cells (the value table, comparison and criteria tables no longer collapse into one column in edit mode).
- `--import` carries view edits into `notes/edits.json` (`views`, newer edit wins, null removes); the next build replaces the view's values, title and history, redraws its SM30 screen from the edited rows and recounts the activity's rows.

## [0.6.36] — 2026-10-15

## [Unreleased]

## [0.6.38] — 2026-10-15

### Added — `interface-mapping-spec`: interface mapping specifications

- New skill `/sc4sap:interface-mapping-spec`: one editable HTML page per interface in the classic mapping-specification layout — cover, revision history, header, systems, Source → Target field grid with conversion-rule (R) and MAPPING columns, an optional response block for synchronous interfaces, conversion rules, extraction condition, remarks and the field guide (ⓘ tooltips). Output: `interfaces/<IF_ID>/<IF_ID>-v<n>-<lang>.html` under the profile artifact base, with an English companion.
- Built for new interfaces: four scenario presets (master data outbound, transaction outbound, inbound into SAP, query) fill the header and the response block; the SAP side comes from a `TABLE-FIELD` / data-element list, from the module consultant's proposal (checked against DDIC), from an Excel paste or an empty grid — or is read from an existing table, DB view, structure (proxy) or function module signature (TABLES parameters named as outputs go to the response block).
- Fields are grouped by the unit they travel in: ▸ group rows per side with name, PARAMETER / STRUCTURE / TABLE and occurrence; a row's Table column holds only the source DDIC table, and the systems' Structure / occurrence is the summary of the groups. Source and target sides have their own colours.
- Proposals: the counterpart side (same names, DB types, MAPPING 1:1), DDIC types shown as DB types (the DDIC type in the tooltip), conversion rules from the field types (dates, times, leading zeros / ALPHA, currency amounts, quantities and units), IF ID numbering from a project pattern. Proposals are marked until edited or confirmed.
- In-page checks: empty required items, MAPPING to a missing row, unknown rule ids, size truncation, type-family and key mismatches, unmapped target fields.
- Edit mode with nothing installed: code lists as drop-downs, rows and groups added / moved / deleted with MAPPING following the renumbering, Excel paste, undo, browser autosave; Save adds the revision row (author, change, approver) and raises the version. `import` takes the page back and fills hand-typed SAP fields from DDIC; `refresh` reads SAP again, keeps what the user wrote and marks added / changed / removed fields; `fields` hands the SAP-side field list to `/sc4sap:create-object`.
- Cover, document-number pattern, ID pattern and code lists per project in `interfaces/project.json`.
